findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the config-presence check in AC2 with a concrete, reliable proving command — e.g., parse `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` output during the manual tickets fetch to confirm the partial-clone filter was applied (filter line present, no blob objects fetched), or assert that `git count-objects -vH` in the worktree shows zero loose/pack objects added after the manual fetch step.

No alternative proving command is offered (e.g., GIT_TRACE2_EVENT log showing a partial-clone filter applied during the fetch, or comparing pack counts before/after the manual fetch in a blobless vs full-clone job).
E6 taxonomy item (4): fixture/check does not actually exercise the claim.
findings.finding: AC2 requires confirming that the manual tickets fetch 'inherits remote.origin.partialclonefilter', but the plan itself explicitly rules out the config-presence check ('git writes partialclonefilter even when the server ignored the filter — reproduced'), and provides no alternative proving command. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a rationale paragraph explaining why `git worktree add` is safe on a blobless runner (it uses `unpack-trees -u` / `check_updates()` which batch-fetches missing promisor blobs in one RPC, unlike `read-tree`/`checkout-index`), so readers can distinguish this path from the attested-materialization footgun documented in `test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py`.
evidence: Plan: 'The subsequent manual tickets fetch is confirmed to inherit remote.origin.partialclonefilter (the mechanism the saving depends on).'
test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py docstring: 'every missing blob becomes its own sequential git fetch RPC — on the ~25k-file tickets tree, hours'
repo_snapshot.py module docstring: 'a clone that filters once keeps filtering forever. An ALREADY-latched clone is repaired by _ensure_blobs_present'
The plan's safety argument covers only verify-identity (tree-level scan from working tree), not the worktree-add checkout step itself
git worktree add uses unpack-trees -u (check_updates() path) which batches promisor fetches — but this is not stated in the plan
findings.finding: The plan asserts that `remote.origin.partialclonefilter` inheritance is 'load-bearing' but does not address the safety of the tickets-branch worktree checkout under a blobless clone. When the inherited filter causes `git fetch origin '+tickets:...'` to deliver commits+trees but no blobs, `git worktree add` must obtain blob content to populate `.tickets-tracker/`. The codebase explicitly documents (test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py, repo_snapshot.py module docstring) that certain git plumbing paths (`read-tree`/`checkout-index`) degrade to per-object lazy fetches on blobless clones — 'hours on a ~25k-file tree'. The plan does not explain why `git worktree add` is safe here (it uses `unpack-trees -u` + `check_updates()` which *does* batch-prefetch promisor blobs, unlike the attested materialization path), leaving the rationale for this safety-critical distinction entirely unstated.
findings.location: "Why blob:none is safe here" section; AC3 (reconciler pass on blobless runner); workflows: git worktree add steps at reconcile-bridge.yml:117, verify-identity.yml:57, reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:88
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer reading the plan cannot verify that the worktree checkout won't degrade to per-blob RPCs, because the plan omits the `unpack-trees` vs `read-tree`/`checkout-index` distinction
If the tickets branch grows large (many event files), a per-blob lazy fetch at worktree-add time would be a regression — the plan gives no bound or argument ruling this out
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Why blob:none is safe here' section, add: '`git worktree add` uses the `unpack-trees -u` plumbing path (`check_updates()`), which batch-prefetches all missing promisor blobs in a single RPC — unlike `git read-tree` (no `-u`) + `checkout-index`, which issue one RPC per missing blob (the footgun documented in `test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py`). So the tickets working-tree checkout remains a single fetch round-trip, not N per-event-file fetches.'

The plan states 'actions/checkout has supported a filter: input since v4.1.0' — this is plausible and consistent with known history, but it is Partially-verified (recalled from training, not observed). findings.finding: The plan introduces a non-obvious CI architectural pattern (blobless clones with filter inheritance across steps) that has at least two documented footguns — server-side filter silently ignored yet partialclonefilter config still written (false-positive config check), and tree:0 measured at 3.4x larger than full clone — but no ADR, AGENTS.md update, or design-doc capture is planned to preserve this reasoning for future maintainers.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief ADR (or an AGENTS.md section under CI) documenting: (1) use blob:none, never tree:0 (cite measurements); (2) config-presence check for partialclonefilter is unreliable — use byte measurement; (3) manual tickets fetch inherits filter from checkout — do not reorder or split these steps. Alternatively, add a block comment in each affected workflow YAML above the checkout step.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the plan's capability note to 'filter: replaces only the internal filter that sparse-checkout applies; both inputs can coexist (see actions/checkout issue #2247)' to avoid misleading future maintainers.
evidence: Plan text: 'Note filter overrides sparse-checkout in that action.'
Official action README (github.com/actions/checkout, all mirrors): 'Partially clone against a given filter. Overrides sparse-checkout if set.' — matches plan wording but is itself imprecise.
Community issue #2247 (actions/checkout): 'adding a filter does not disable sparse-checkout. It just overrides the filter that is automatically applied when sparse-checkout is set'
starsling.dev (actions/checkout v7 reference): 'an explicit filter only replaces the filter it applies for you, so you can set both'
None of the three target workflows currently use sparse-checkout, so no runtime defect arises from this plan; the risk is future-maintainer confusion.
findings.finding: The plan states 'Note filter overrides sparse-checkout in that action' as a factual capability assertion. The official action README does carry this wording, but community issue #2247 and the action's implementation clarify that filter: only replaces the *internal filter* that sparse-checkout applies for you — it does not disable sparse-checkout itself, and both inputs can coexist. The plan's imprecise framing could mislead future maintainers who want to combine filter: blob:none with sparse-checkout on these workflows.
findings.location: Plan section: 'actions/checkout has supported a filter: input since v4.1.0. Note filter overrides sparse-checkout in that action.'
scenarios: A future maintainer reads the plan's note, concludes filter: and sparse-checkout are mutually exclusive, and avoids combining them when that would be the right solution for a different optimization.
The plan's note is copied into a comment in the workflow YAML, creating persistent misleading documentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Note filter overrides sparse-checkout in that action.' with: 'Note: filter: replaces only the internal blob filter that sparse-checkout applies under the hood; filter: and sparse-checkout: can coexist (actions/checkout issue #2247). None of the three target workflows use sparse-checkout, so this is not a concern here.'
